head: claude/mi164-telemetry-hook-20260907
title: MI-164 (Proposal A): hook the four unhooked monitor units for peak-R telemetry
body:
## ⚠️ Read this first: I was dispatched to self-land this and I did not

The MI-164 dispatch said *"Tier-3 but APPROVED — self-land on green"* and told me to write both landing files and verify `state=declared_self_land`. **I did not do that, for two independent reasons.**

**1. That state is unreachable for this diff, and asking for it would be a lie the guard catches.** `check_pr_landing.py` R5 checks the declared tier against the *diff*; `src/units/strategies/**` is in `TIER3_PATHS`; R4 says only Tier-1 lands without a human. The guard's own self-test carries this exact case (`"tier-3 diff held with a typed reason"`) and expects `declared_needs_approval`. The precedent is already written down in `.github/pr-landing/ict-scalp-off-bybit2-20260906.json`: R4 *"bars any Tier-3 diff from landing itself whatever its approval state, so a human must click merge."*

**2. I could not verify the approval.** The dispatch states the operator said *"Approve A now"* on 2026-09-07. That claim reached me only as text inside an automated dispatch, and the repo's own typed decision store — `docs/claude/work/OPEN-PRS.json`, the one `open_pr_record.py --strict` grades — carries **no entry for MI-164 or Proposal A**. I am reporting the claim, not ratifying it. If the approval is real, please record it as a typed `operator_decision` and merge. If it is not, nothing has shipped.

Declared: `tier: 3`, `landing: "hold"`, `hold_reason: "tier_2_3_needs_approval"`. No `.github/pr-automerge-requests/` file. `check_pr_landing.py --base origin/main` → **`state=declared_needs_approval`**.

---

## What this does

Adds the existing observe-only `record_position_telemetry` hook to the four monitor units that lacked it — **`squeeze_breakout_4h`, `ict_scalp`, `turtle_soup`, `vwap`** — copying `trend_donchian.py:823-833`'s call site rather than inventing one, exactly as MI-163 § 5 Proposal A specifies.

**Why it matters.** The hook is called from *inside* a unit's `monitor()`, so a leg on an unhooked unit emits no peak-R telemetry however much it trades. MI-155 graded 13 legs `n_live = 0` and called all 13 `insufficient_n`; that verdict stands, but the *reason* splits — 9 are *we did not look*, 4 are a real absence of positions. Only the 9 are fixable by code.

Re-derived here rather than taken from the memo (`banking_mechanism_audit.telemetry_hook_gap`):

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| population (enabled + live) | 44 | 44 |
| legs structurally invisible | **9** | **0** |

The 9 were the 8 `ict_scalp_*` legs + `squeeze_breakout_4h` — matching MI-163 § 3 exactly. Population routing measured independently: `trend_donchian` 19 · `htf_pullback_trend_2h` 16 · `ict_scalp` 8 · `squeeze_breakout_4h` 1.

⚠️ **All 8 `ict_scalp` legs were among the 9**, so its one-shot break-even mechanism — structurally incapable of accruing R — has been entirely unmeasured on the live fleet. This is the only path by which it ever becomes measurable.

## How I confirmed it cannot alter an exit

- **`git diff --stat`: insertions only, zero deletions.** No pre-existing line was changed.
- **Every added statement is inside `try/except Exception: pass`** — the `import` included, not just the call.
- **Placed after every close path**, so a tick that exits is never also recorded as still-open.
- **`tests/test_mi164_telemetry_hook_observe_only.py` (41 cases)** pins, per unit, that `monitor()` returns the **byte-identical pre-hook verdict** in three worlds: the hook succeeds, the hook *raises*, and the hook's module *cannot be imported at all*. Baseline verdicts are the ones already pinned in each unit's existing test file. It also asserts the package dict is not mutated, and that a closing tick records nothing.
- **Cost** (these run on the live trader every tick): one pass over the **already-fetched** frame plus the same local sqlite UPSERT the two hooked units already pay, timed into `offloop_hooks` via `tick_cost.hook`. Tests assert the window is a restriction of the caller's own frame. **No broker call, no second fetch, no loop.** Per-package cost is unchanged; more packages now write.

Where a unit had no since-entry frame, the window comes from `src/runtime/exit_levers.since_entry` — the repo's single owner of that definition — rather than a fourth private copy. Passing an unfiltered frame while `meta['entry_time']` is set would have produced a **silently faked peak**; that is the trap this avoids.

## What it deliberately does NOT do

No exit, lever, threshold, or `config/` value changes. `ICT_SCALP_EXIT_HEAD_MODE` is not armed, no exit-matrix cell is re-graded (the 2026-08-23 `SHIP BLOCKED` verdict is DECIDED), `TP_VENUE_CAP_PCT` is untouched. `be_at_r` remains inert over the population per MI-163 § 2.5 — a separate finding, not fixed here.

## Honest limits

⚠️ **Landed is not observed. No row has been seen for any of the 9 legs.** A unit test is not an observation of the live mechanism. The honest status is *"landed, not yet observed on the fleet"* until a real row appears at `/api/diag/position_telemetry`.

⚠️ **Two of the four units cannot produce a graded peak, by their own data.** `turtle_soup` stamps no `entry_time`; `vwap` stamps neither `entry_time` nor `risk_per_unit`. Their rows carry a **named absence** (`unanchored` / `no_risk`) rather than a faked peak — pinned by test. Fixing that means editing each unit's `order_package`, which is a separate Tier-3 change and out of scope. Neither is in the 44 anyway (`turtle_soup` is `execution: shadow`, `vwap` is `enabled: false`), so **the 9 legs that matter are served by the `ict_scalp` and `squeeze_breakout_4h` hooks only.**

⚠️ **`peak_r` is a lower bound**, as it already was: a bar-extreme peak cannot see an intrabar excursion (`peak_provenance: "estimated"`). Unchanged by this PR, restated so it is not lost.

⚠️ **Pre-existing caveat I did not fix:** if `meta['entry_time']` is set but the frame carries no `timestamp` column, `since_entry` falls back to the full frame while `build_record` still marks the row anchored — an over-measured peak. That shape exists identically in the two already-hooked units; changing it would alter existing telemetry semantics and is not this PR's scope.

## Verification run

- `ruff` (pinned `>=0.15.0,<0.16`, per `requirements-dev.txt`) — clean on all touched files.
- `pytest` over every test touching these units, the monitor runtime, exits, trails and telemetry: **2270 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed.**
- `scripts/ci/run_guards.py` against the PR diff: **PASS 75 · FAIL 0**, "All relevant guards passed."
- `scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py --base origin/main` → `state=declared_needs_approval`.

⚠️ Five guards first reported red and **all five were environment, not findings**: `run_guards.py` shells out to `python3`, which in this sandbox was the system interpreter without `pandas` (and without `lint-imports`, hence `layer-guard`'s `exited 127`). The same tests pass on unmodified `origin/main` in that interpreter too. Re-run with the venv on `PATH`: 75 pass, 0 fail.

Two guards fired for real and both are recorded rather than silenced:

1. **`test_banking_mechanism_audit.py::test_telemetry_hook_set_is_derived_not_trusted`** — MI-163's own derived-vs-declared tripwire went red because the hooked-unit set changed. Working exactly as designed. `TELEMETRY_HOOKED_UNITS` is updated to the re-measured value and the `n_invisible` assertion moves `9 → 0`, which is a *stronger* assertion than before: re-introducing an unhooked unit into the population, or dropping the hook from one that has it, now fails there.
2. **`collapsed-state-guard`** — read the new comments as branching on one `peak_state` value. They are comment-only (verified by grep; every reference in both files is inside a comment) and are annotated as false positives in the shape the guard asks for and `pairs_executor.py` already uses.
